AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Diverse methods have been developed for intraoperative monitoring of the integrity of the visual pathways. We performed a review of the literature to determine the methodology of each technique as well as their recent development. The predictive power of each eligible technique was determined based on a meta-analysis.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A review of the literature was performed according to PRISMA statement. The techniques, which were adopted for intraoperative monitoring of the integrity of the visual pathways, were extracted and described. The power of each eligible technique to predict the visual outcome was tested.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The visual evoked potentials showed recently marked methodological improvement. The predictive power for visual deterioration after surgery was about 60% and reached 100% when coupled with simultaneous monitoring of electroretinography (ERG). The sensitivity of the VEPs for detection of deterioration was 47.2%. The decrease of the fractional anisotropy of the optic chiasma showed significant correlation with the improvement of the vision after chiasma compression and showed 100% predictive power for improvement.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Each technique has its own limitation. VEPs have a high peridctive power for detection of deterioaration but with low sensitivity. The fractional anisotropy of the optic chiasma has a high predictive power for improvement of vision with low predictive power for deterioration.
